title: Domain Modelling and Data Relationships
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Domain Modelling and Data Relationships.
Apply domain modelling and data relationships to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to domain modelling and data relationships.
Review common mistakes and risks in domain modelling and data relationships.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using domain modelling and data relationships principles.

understand.concept: Domain modelling identifies important concepts and relationships in a problem. A model captures attributes, identifiers, invariants and operations without depending prematurely on a database or user interface.
understand.whyItMatters: A shared model reduces inconsistent representations and clarifies business rules.
understand.analogy: A map represents important places and connections needed for a journey, not every physical detail.
understand.analogyLimit: A model is a purposeful simplification and evolves as requirements become clearer.
understand.summary: Domain Modelling and Data Relationships helps learners plan and deliver maintainable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Identify entities, value objects and relationships. Write invariants that must always hold. Use Python classes or dataclasses when they clarify the model, but keep persistence and presentation outside the domain model.

examples.title: Domain record
examples.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass
class Book:
    isbn: str
    title: str
book = Book('B1', 'Python Basics')
print(book.title)
examples.explanation: A dataclass represents a domain entity.

examples.title: Relationship
examples.explanation: A loan connects a member and a book.

examples.title: Invariant
examples.code:
def can_loan(available): return available > 0
print(can_loan(1), can_loan(0))
examples.explanation: The rule prevents lending unavailable stock.

practise.guidedTask: Model a library with Book, Member and Loan concepts, relationships and invariants.
practise.independentTask: Sketch an inventory and billing domain model.
hints: Find nouns and actions in requirements.
Write invariants in plain language first.
Avoid coupling domain objects to database rows or UI widgets.
practise.challenge: Create a course-enrolment model that prevents duplicate enrolment.
validationCriteria: The project concept is accurately explained and applied.
All examples execute with documented output on Python 3.13.
The proposed artifact is testable and appropriate to stated requirements.
Trade-offs, limitations and relevant risks are acknowledged.
